summary: Main claim: the railed Hubble-constant posterior of an independently implemented Gray-et-al.-family galaxy-catalogue dark-siren estimator (simulated LISA EMRI campaign at injected h=0.73 against the real GLADE+ catalogue) is a curable prior-consistency artifact of the completion-term normalization, not photometric information starvation -- restoring the isotropic 1/(4pi) sky marginal flips the rail from h=0.86 to h=0.60, and either prior-consistent repair (local ratio-of-sums or comoving-volume kernel deconvolution) de-rails the posterior to an interior peak at the injected truth on identical data, while synthetic known-truth tests show the bare-Gaussian kernel carries an Eddington-type sigma_z^2 bias that collapses frequentist coverage. The paper's logic is a coherent diagnose-predict-test arc (three defects -> sign-flip prediction -> de-rail matrix + ablation -> coverage calibration -> field-level audit) with unusually disciplined scope statements and per-number artifact sourcing. Strongest suspected narrative weaknesses: (1) the manuscript is literally incomplete -- the full-grid, full-sample confirmation of the headline de-rail is an explicit [RESULT PENDING] placeholder; (2) regime bookkeeping: the abstract frames the work as probing the sigma_z/z ~ 0.7 regime, but the paper's own coverage calibration lives at sigma_z/z ~ 0.1-0.2 (sigma_z=0.035, median detected z~0.3) and the real-data section states most GLADE+ hosts in the sample carry near-spectroscopic uncertainties, so the headline regime is probed only by a subset and never receives a coverage test at that ratio; (3) an apparent internal tension in the real-data section between 'for 3331 of 3355 events the in-catalogue completion numerator evaluates to zero' and the same section's conclusion that 'the in-catalogue information was present all along'.
strengths: Disciplined scope statements: the paper repeatedly and prominently states that events are simulated, that every claim concerns estimator calibration against a known injected truth, and it discloses the dt^2 SNR-scale defect of the seed600 sample rather than hiding it.

A falsifiable sign-flip prediction (up-rail -> down-rail -> interior peak) stated before the test and then observed on identical data, with a two-factor ablation cleanly separating kernel consistency (the de-railing factor) from the global-vs-local denominator (the residual +0.03).

Independent, deterministic, released P-P/coverage harness (no production-code imports, paired per-realization seeds, regression-pinned), giving the calibration claim a defensible independence argument.
Quantitative mechanism verification: the Eddington-in-z sigma_z^2 law is checked against measured biases across a factor 11 in sigma_z^2 with a stable implied coefficient, not just asserted.

Term-by-term mapping onto the published Gray et al. equations with every deviation declared as deliberate rather than silently absorbed, plus an honest partial-fix matrix in the postmortem including its own failed repairs.
A systematic-error budget with explicit dispositions (fixed / quoted / campaign) and magnitudes, including items unfavourable to the authors (timeout selection, Omega_m fiducial).

findings.summary: The manuscript contains an explicit [RESULT PENDING] placeholder for the full-scale confirmation (all 3375 events, 38-value grid, volume_deconv default); the headline de-rail evidence therefore currently rests entirely on a 494-event subsample and a seven-point grid.
findings.rationale: This is an acknowledged, intentional placeholder (cluster jobs 5698617/5698618 queued), not a hidden omission, and the paper is honest that the matrix rests on the subsample. But a manuscript cannot go to referees with a pending central-confirmation slot, and if the full-grid result were not peaked near 0.73 the de-rail narrative would need revision. Recorded as pending evidence, not as misconduct.
findings.required_action: Fill the placeholder with the actual full-grid combined-posterior result before any submission decision; if the result deviates from the expected interior peak near 0.73, revise the de-rail claims accordingly.

findings.summary: Regime bookkeeping between the headline sigma_z/z ~ 0.7 framing and the evidence actually presented: the abstract says 'sigma_z/z ~ 0.7 in the GLADE+ regime probed here', but the coverage calibration runs at sigma_z = 0.035 with median detected z ~ 0.3 (sigma_z/z ~ 0.12, spanning ~0.1-0.2 over the detected population), and the real-data section states most GLADE+ hosts in the sample carry near-spectroscopic redshift uncertainties.
findings.rationale: The validation gap the paper identifies (no known-truth calibration at sigma_z/z ~ 0.7, catalogue-dominated) is precise, but the paper's own known-truth coverage test does not occupy that regime either: it demonstrates calibration at photometric absolute width sigma_z = 0.035 at redshifts where the ratio is ~0.1-0.2. The sigma_z/z ~ 0.7 figure is realized only for the low-z photometric subset (e.g. z_g = 0.05 with sigma_z = 0.035) inside a sample dominated by near-spectroscopic hosts. Abstract and conclusions juxtapose the gap statement with the paper's coverage tests in a way that invites reading the harness as closing the sigma_z/z ~ 0.7 gap, which is stronger than what is shown. This is central to the significance framing, so it cannot be deferred as presentation polish.
findings.required_action: State explicitly, in the abstract and wherever the sigma_z/z ~ 0.7 gap is invoked, which sigma_z/z each piece of evidence occupies (coverage tests: absolute sigma_z = 0.035 at sigma_z/z ~ 0.1-0.2; real-data sample: mixed, mostly near-spectroscopic, photometric subset reaching ~0.7), and either add a coverage run at sigma_z/z ~ 0.7 or narrow the closing-the-gap language to 'a first step at photometric absolute width'.

findings.summary: The abstract's unqualified 'the volume-deconvolved kernel is calibrated close to nominal' is supported only in the clean single-host limit; inside the full completion machinery the corrected estimator's synthetic coverage is 0.40/0.54/0.82 with a residual -0.013 bias and a compressed MAP-vs-truth slope of ~0.35 shared by all non-railing variants.
findings.rationale: Section 5.3 discloses these residuals and attributes them to the synthetic's completeness/interloper modelling, declaring the clean single-host test 'the decisive calibration verdict' -- but that decisiveness is asserted, not demonstrated. Since the real-data configuration is completion-dominated (w_G = 0.8175 but the completion channel carries most of the constraint per Section 6), calibration of the full machinery, not just the single-host limit, is what the real-data claim needs. The abstract-level claim should be scoped.
findings.required_action: Scope the calibration claim in the abstract/conclusions to the clean single-host limit, or provide evidence (not attribution) that the full-machinery residuals are properties of the synthetic's completeness/interloper modelling rather than of the estimator.

findings.summary: Apparent internal tension in Section 6: 'for 3331 of the 3355 events the in-catalogue completion numerator evaluates to zero at working precision' sits in the same section as 'the in-catalogue information was present all along' and a catalogue-only configuration (completion term discarded) that peaks at 0.73.
findings.rationale: If the in-catalogue channel is zero for 99.3 per cent of events, it is unclear what carries the catalogue-only constraint, unless (a) the 494-event subsample was chosen to have non-zero in-catalogue terms, (b) 'in-catalogue completion numerator' denotes a different object than the in-catalogue likelihood term (the phrase is ambiguous -- it reads as a hybrid of the two channels), or (c) the zeroing applies only in a particular configuration. As written, the statement appears to undercut the central 'information was present all along' narrative and needs disambiguation before technical review can adjudicate it.
findings.required_action: Define precisely which quantity evaluates to zero for 3331/3355 events and in which configuration, state how the 494-event subsample was selected relative to that zeroing, and reconcile the statement with the catalogue-only row of Table 2.

findings.summary: The abstract and conclusions quote 'interior peak at the injected truth, h = 0.73' without noting that the de-rail matrix uses a seven-point grid that contains 0.73 as a grid point with +-0.03 neighbours, so peak-location agreement is demonstrated only at that resolution.
findings.rationale: The body is candid ('computational economy', 'coarse seven-point grid', full 38-point confirmation pending), and the posterior means (0.730, 0.740) add support beyond the MAP. But the abstract-level phrasing implies a precision the grid cannot deliver until the pending full-grid run lands.
findings.required_action: Either qualify the abstract claim with the grid resolution, or update it with the full 38-point-grid result once available (which also resolves REF-R001).

findings.summary: The negative universal novelty claim ('no published pipeline has a known-truth calibration test at sigma_z/z ~ 0.7, catalogue-dominated') survives only under its precise two-condition conjunction, and the paper itself cites CHIMERA's known-truth photometric mocks (sigma_z = 0.05(1+z), broadened-but-unbiased H0) that approach the gap.
findings.rationale: Section 8 draws the boundary carefully (CHIMERA's mocks are known-truth and photometric but at sigma_z/z below ~0.5 and arguably not catalogue-information-dominated), but the abstract and conclusions restate the claim without the full conjunction. Negative-existence claims across a field are fragile and rest here on the authors' own four-pipeline pinned-version audit; the literature stage must verify no other known-truth photometric calibration exists (including post-audit gwcosmo LOS work and any mock data challenges).
findings.required_action: Restate the novelty claim with its full conjunction (known-truth AND catalogue-information-dominated AND sigma_z/z ~ 0.7) everywhere it appears; literature stage to independently verify the negative claim.

findings.summary: The framework section declares 'All redshifts z are CMB-frame redshifts', but the budget section discloses that the committed baselines of Section 6 used heliocentric redshifts (measured net effect ~ +0.15 per cent on H0).
findings.rationale: The discrepancy is disclosed and quantified as negligible against the Delta-MAP ~ 0.1 effects at issue, but the framework's blanket convention statement is contradicted by the actual data underlying the headline tables; a one-line qualification in Section 2 or 6 would fix it.
findings.required_action: Qualify the CMB-frame convention statement to note that the Section 6 baselines predate the catalogue rebuild and used heliocentric redshifts, with the quoted +0.15 per cent effect.

findings.summary: Submission placeholders remain: author 'TBD', affiliation 'TBD', and acknowledgements 'TBD --- funding, compute ... collaborators'.
findings.rationale: Purely administrative, but the manuscript cannot be submitted with these in place; recording so the pre-submission checklist catches them.
findings.required_action: Fill author list, affiliations, and acknowledgements before submission.

findings.summary: Minor grid inconsistency across sections: the de-rail matrix uses h in [0.60, 0.86] (rail at 0.86) while the postmortem's full-sample bare run uses a 0.01-spaced grid on [0.60, 0.87] (rail at 0.87); Table 4's caption discloses the mixed provenance but the abstract quotes only the [0.60, 0.86] grid.
findings.rationale: Both rails are edge results and the paper explicitly warns that unconstrained maxima may lie outside the grid, so no substantive issue -- but harmonizing or footnoting the two grids would remove a small reader stumble.
findings.required_action: Add a one-line note reconciling the [0.60, 0.86] seven-point diagnostic grid with the [0.60, 0.87] 0.01-spaced full-sample grid.
